notes: Civil War: Wikipedia lists both lines (Confederate: Moore to 1864-01-25, then Henry Watkins Allen 1864-01-25 to 1865-06-02; Union: Shepley, Hahn, Wells). New Orleans fell 1862-04-25 and Baton Rouge was occupied in May 1862; Moore's government fled to Opelousas/Shreveport. Used the Union line from Shepley's appointment (1862-07-02): Moore's end truncated to 1862-07-02 and Allen excluded.

Shepley (1862-07-02 to 1864-03-04) was a Union military governor (Wikipedia party cell: 'Military governor'); recorded with party_raw None and military_appointee true. Flanders and Baker (1867-1868) were 'Appointed by military occupation'; also party_raw None.
1873 dual government: John McEnery (Democratic, 1873-01-13 to 1873-05-22) excluded; William Pitt Kellogg (Republican) held the statehouse in New Orleans with federal recognition and troops.

1877 dual government: Stephen B. Packard (Republican, 1877-01-08 to 1877-04-25) excluded. Packard was confined to the St. Louis Hotel statehouse under federal protection while Francis T. Nicholls' (Democratic) government took control of New Orleans and the state; judgment call, Nicholls used from 1877-01-08.
Michael Hahn's party is labelled 'Union Free Trade (Republican)' and James Madison Wells' is 'Citizens Ticket' (linked to the Louisiana Democratic Party; colour cell Democratic). Kept as labelled.
Henry Clay Warmoth: first ~16 days (1868-06-27 appointment to 1868-07-13 inauguration) labelled 'Appointed by military occupation'; recorded as Republican for the whole term.
Buddy Roemer was elected as a Democrat and switched to Republican late in his term (1991); Wikipedia labels him Democratic, kept as Democratic.
Murphy J. Foster labelled 'Anti-Lottery Democratic'.

John H. Reed (1959-12-30) succeeded as President of the Senate acting, then won the 1960 special and 1962 elections; recorded as one non-acting term. Senate presidents who only served out a vacancy are acting: true.
James B. Longley and Angus King are labelled 'Independent'.

Mandel (1969-01-07 to 1979-01-17 in the table) designated Lt. Gov. Blair Lee III acting governor 1977-06-04 to 1979-01-15; Mandel split into two terms around Lee's acting term. Lee was briefly acting again on 1979-01-16 (ignored).

Roger Wolcott (1896), Francis Sargent (1969) and Paul Cellucci (1997) began as Lieutenant governor acting and were later elected; recorded as one non-acting term each. Thomas Talbot (1874-75) and Jane Swift (2001-03) were acting only.
Henry Gardner (in office 1856-01-01) labelled 'Know Nothing'.
Michigan list uses January 1 for most inaugurations; recorded as given (day precision).
Statehood 1858-05-11; first state governor Henry Hastings Sibley took office 1858-05-24 (13-day gap, territorial governor Samuel Medary excluded).

Party labels: Wikipedia displays 'Democratic-Farmer-Labor' / 'Farmer-Labor' with hyphens in the governor rows (links go to 'Democratic–Farmer–Labor Party' / 'Farmer–Labor Party'); recorded with en dashes as 'Democratic–Farmer–Labor' and 'Farmer–Labor'. Al Quie and Arne Carlson labelled 'Independent-Republican' (the MN GOP's name 1975-1995). Jesse Ventura labelled 'Reform/Independence' (Reform Party of Minnesota, renamed Independence Party in 2000).

notes: Gap 1865-05-22 (Charles Clark removed by Union forces) to 1865-06-13 (Sharkey appointed) filled with a '(military rule)' term.

William L. Sharkey (1865) 'Provisional governor appointed by President' and Adelbert Ames (1868-1870) 'Provisional governor appointed by military occupation' recorded with party_raw None (wiki_label holds the exact text). Ames's later 1874-1876 term is Republican.
Benjamin G. Humphreys (1865-1868) labelled 'Non-partisan' (the 1865 election was officially non-partisan).
John Marshall Stone (1876) and Fielding L. Wright (1946) succeeded as acting and were later elected; recorded as one non-acting term each.
Confederate governors Pettus and Clark kept per the main list; no rival Union civil government is listed for Mississippi.

Civil War: Claiborne Fox Jackson (Democratic, pro-Confederate) ended 1861-07-31 when the state convention replaced him with Hamilton Rowan Gamble (Union, provisional) in Jefferson City. The Confederate government-in-exile (Jackson, then Thomas Caute Reynolds) is not in the main list and is excluded.
Benjamin Gratz Brown labelled 'Liberal Republican'; Gamble and Willard P. Hall labelled 'Union'.
